import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, cross_val_score
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, roc_auc_score

# Production machine learning implementation: Why Model Interpretability Matters
def train_and_evaluate_model(X: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.Series):
    # 1. Stratified train/test partition to preserve class distributions
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
        X, y, test_size=0.20, random_state=42, stratify=y
    )
    
    # 2. Fit feature scaler on training data ONLY to prevent data leakage
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
    X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)
    
    # 3. Model instantiation with ensemble regularization
    clf = RandomForestClassifier(
        n_estimators=150, max_depth=10, min_samples_split=5, random_state=42
    )
    clf.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)
    
    # 4. Out-of-sample evaluation
    y_pred = clf.predict(X_test_scaled)
    y_proba = clf.predict_proba(X_test_scaled)[:, 1]
    
    print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred))
    print(f"ROC-AUC Score: {roc_auc_score(y_test, y_proba):.4f}")
    return clf, scaler

codeSnippet.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.optim as optim

# Production PyTorch architecture: What Is Deep Learning?
class DeepClassifier(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_dim: int, hidden_dim: int, num_classes: int):
        super().__init__()
        self.network = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(hidden_dim),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Dropout(p=0.25),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim // 2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim // 2, num_classes)
        )

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return self.network(x)

# Training step with AdamW optimizer & Cross-Entropy Loss
device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
model = DeepClassifier(input_dim=64, hidden_dim=128, num_classes=5).to(device)
criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
optimizer = optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3, weight_decay=1e-4)

items.title: Biological Neurons vs Artificial Neurons
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to biological neurons vs artificial neurons with mathematical derivations, neural architecture diagrams, production code, and real-world evaluation.

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, cross_val_score
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, roc_auc_score

# Production machine learning implementation: Biological Neurons vs Artificial Neurons
def train_and_evaluate_model(X: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.Series):
    # 1. Stratified train/test partition to preserve class distributions
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
        X, y, test_size=0.20, random_state=42, stratify=y
    )
    
    # 2. Fit feature scaler on training data ONLY to prevent data leakage
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
    X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)
    
    # 3. Model instantiation with ensemble regularization
    clf = RandomForestClassifier(
        n_estimators=150, max_depth=10, min_samples_split=5, random_state=42
    )
    clf.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)
    
    # 4. Out-of-sample evaluation
    y_pred = clf.predict(X_test_scaled)
    y_proba = clf.predict_proba(X_test_scaled)[:, 1]
    
    print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred))
    print(f"ROC-AUC Score: {roc_auc_score(y_test, y_proba):.4f}")
    return clf, scaler

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, cross_val_score
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, roc_auc_score

# Production machine learning implementation: Forward Propagation
def train_and_evaluate_model(X: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.Series):
    # 1. Stratified train/test partition to preserve class distributions
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
        X, y, test_size=0.20, random_state=42, stratify=y
    )
    
    # 2. Fit feature scaler on training data ONLY to prevent data leakage
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
    X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)
    
    # 3. Model instantiation with ensemble regularization
    clf = RandomForestClassifier(
        n_estimators=150, max_depth=10, min_samples_split=5, random_state=42
    )
    clf.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)
    
    # 4. Out-of-sample evaluation
    y_pred = clf.predict(X_test_scaled)
    y_proba = clf.predict_proba(X_test_scaled)[:, 1]
    
    print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred))
    print(f"ROC-AUC Score: {roc_auc_score(y_test, y_proba):.4f}")
    return clf, scaler

codeSnippet.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.optim as optim

# Production PyTorch architecture: Backpropagation
class DeepClassifier(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_dim: int, hidden_dim: int, num_classes: int):
        super().__init__()
        self.network = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(hidden_dim),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Dropout(p=0.25),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim // 2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim // 2, num_classes)
        )

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return self.network(x)

# Training step with AdamW optimizer & Cross-Entropy Loss
device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
model = DeepClassifier(input_dim=64, hidden_dim=128, num_classes=5).to(device)
criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
optimizer = optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3, weight_decay=1e-4)

codeSnippet.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.optim as optim

# Production PyTorch architecture: Introduction to PyTorch
class DeepClassifier(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_dim: int, hidden_dim: int, num_classes: int):
        super().__init__()
        self.network = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(hidden_dim),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Dropout(p=0.25),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim // 2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim // 2, num_classes)
        )

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return self.network(x)

# Training step with AdamW optimizer & Cross-Entropy Loss
device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
model = DeepClassifier(input_dim=64, hidden_dim=128, num_classes=5).to(device)
criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
optimizer = optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3, weight_decay=1e-4)

codeSnippet.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.optim as optim

# Production PyTorch architecture: Building a Neural Network
class DeepClassifier(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_dim: int, hidden_dim: int, num_classes: int):
        super().__init__()
        self.network = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(hidden_dim),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Dropout(p=0.25),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim // 2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim // 2, num_classes)
        )

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return self.network(x)

# Training step with AdamW optimizer & Cross-Entropy Loss
device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
model = DeepClassifier(input_dim=64, hidden_dim=128, num_classes=5).to(device)
criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
optimizer = optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3, weight_decay=1e-4)

# Production PyTorch architecture: Building a Neural Network for Tabular Data
class DeepClassifier(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_dim: int, hidden_dim: int, num_classes: int):

        self.network = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(hidden_dim),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Dropout(p=0.25),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim // 2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim // 2, num_classes)
        )

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return self.network(x)

# Training step with AdamW optimizer & Cross-Entropy Loss

codeSnippet.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.optim as optim

# Production PyTorch architecture: Building an End-to-End Deep Learning Project
class DeepClassifier(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_dim: int, hidden_dim: int, num_classes: int):
        super().__init__()
        self.network = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(hidden_dim),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Dropout(p=0.25),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim // 2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim // 2, num_classes)
        )

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return self.network(x)

# Training step with AdamW optimizer & Cross-Entropy Loss
device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
model = DeepClassifier(input_dim=64, hidden_dim=128, num_classes=5).to(device)
criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
optimizer = optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3, weight_decay=1e-4)

            nn.BatchNorm1d(hidden_dim),

            nn.Dropout(p=0.25),

    # 1. Stratified train/test partition to preserve class distributions

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.optim as optim

# Production PyTorch architecture: Building a Neural Network for Tabular Data
class DeepClassifier(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_dim: int, hidden_dim: int, num_classes: int):
        super().__init__()
        self.network = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(hidden_dim),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Dropout(p=0.25),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim // 2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim // 2, num_classes)
        )

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return self.network(x)

# Training step with AdamW optimizer & Cross-Entropy Loss
device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
model = DeepClassifier(input_dim=64, hidden_dim=128, num_classes=5).to(device)
criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
optimizer = optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3, weight_decay=1e-4)

    # 4. Out-of-sample evaluation

# Production PyTorch architecture: Building an End-to-End Deep Learning Project

            nn.BatchNorm1d(hidden_dim),

# Training step with AdamW optimizer & Cross-Entropy Loss

questions.prompt: Which fundamental objective guides effective model training and parameter optimization in Deep Learning and Neural Networks?

options.label: Minimizing training loss to exactly zero while ignoring generalization error
Minimizing empirical loss while regularizing model complexity to optimize out-of-sample generalization
Disabling validation splits to reduce GPU compute usage
Maximizing parameter weights without penalty boundaries

questions.explanation: The core objective in machine learning is structural risk minimization: balancing empirical loss reduction with regularization to ensure the model generalizes effectively to unobserved production distributions.

questions.prompt: In Deep Learning and Neural Networks, what is the consequence of severe class imbalance if evaluated solely using standard accuracy?

options.label: The model will automatically recalibrate its probability thresholds without code
A naive model predicting only the majority class can achieve deceptive 99% accuracy while having zero utility
The optimizer will fail to compute gradients during backpropagation
The GPU memory footprint will increase exponentially

questions.explanation: On imbalanced datasets (such as 99% non-fraud vs 1% fraud), a model that predicts non-fraud 100% of the time achieves 99% accuracy while failing completely at detecting fraud. PR-AUC and F1-score are necessary.

questions.prompt: When configuring numerical optimizers like Adam or SGD with momentum in Deep Learning and Neural Networks, why is learning rate selection critical?

options.label: Learning rate has no mathematical effect on convergence speed
Too high a rate causes loss divergence; too low a rate causes agonizingly slow convergence or entrapment in poor local minima
Learning rate only applies to linear regression models
A learning rate of 1.0 is universally optimal for all neural network architectures

questions.explanation: Learning rate dictates step size across the loss landscape gradient. Excessive step sizes overshoot minima and diverge, while excessively small step sizes cause stagnation or freeze in suboptimal saddle points.

questions.prompt: In deep learning architectures for Deep Learning and Neural Networks, what is the primary role of non-linear activation functions (e.g. ReLU, GELU)?

options.label: To convert 32-bit floats into integer strings
To allow neural networks to approximate non-linear functional relationships and avoid collapsing into a single linear mapping
To reduce the physical storage size of saved checkpoint files
To guarantee that all gradients equal zero during backpropagation

questions.explanation: Without non-linear activations, composing multiple linear layers (W2 * W1 * x) mathematically collapses into a single linear matrix transformation (W_eff * x), preventing the network from learning complex non-linear patterns.

questions.prompt: When deploying models in production for Deep Learning and Neural Networks, what is the best strategy for detecting data drift over time?

Continuously monitoring statistical feature divergence (e.g. Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, PSI) between training and live inference payloads
Deleting incoming production payloads after scoring without logging
Disabling API rate limits on inference endpoints

questions.explanation: Production data drift occurs when real-world distributions evolve away from training baseline assumptions. Statistical drift tests (PSI, KS-test) detect these shifts early and trigger automated retraining pipelines.

items.title: What Is Computer Vision?
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to what is computer vision? with mathematical derivations, neural architecture diagrams, production code, and real-world evaluation.

codeSnippet.code:
import cv2
import numpy as np
import torch
import torchvision.transforms as transforms

# Computer vision processing: What Is Computer Vision?
def preprocess_and_infer(image_path: str, target_size=(224, 224)) -> torch.Tensor:
    # 1. Load image in BGR and convert to RGB
    img = cv2.imread(image_path)
    img_rgb = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
    
    # 2. PyTorch tensor normalization pipeline (ImageNet stats)
    transform = transforms.Compose([
        transforms.ToPILImage(),
        transforms.Resize(target_size),
        transforms.ToTensor(),
        transforms.Normalize(mean=[0.485, 0.456, 0.406], std=[0.229, 0.224, 0.225])
    ])
    tensor = transform(img_rgb).unsqueeze(0) # Add batch dimension: (1, 3, 224, 224)
    return tensor

import cv2
import numpy as np
import torch
import torchvision.transforms as transforms

# Computer vision processing: Introduction to OpenCV
def preprocess_and_infer(image_path: str, target_size=(224, 224)) -> torch.Tensor:
    # 1. Load image in BGR and convert to RGB
    img = cv2.imread(image_path)
    img_rgb = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
    
    # 2. PyTorch tensor normalization pipeline (ImageNet stats)
    transform = transforms.Compose([
        transforms.ToPILImage(),
        transforms.Resize(target_size),
        transforms.ToTensor(),
        transforms.Normalize(mean=[0.485, 0.456, 0.406], std=[0.229, 0.224, 0.225])
    ])
    tensor = transform(img_rgb).unsqueeze(0) # Add batch dimension: (1, 3, 224, 224)
    return tensor

items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to convolution operations and filters with mathematical derivations, neural architecture diagrams, production code, and real-world evaluation.

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, cross_val_score
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, roc_auc_score

# Production machine learning implementation: Convolution Operations and Filters
def train_and_evaluate_model(X: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.Series):
    # 1. Stratified train/test partition to preserve class distributions
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
        X, y, test_size=0.20, random_state=42, stratify=y
    )
    
    # 2. Fit feature scaler on training data ONLY to prevent data leakage
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
    X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)
    
    # 3. Model instantiation with ensemble regularization
    clf = RandomForestClassifier(
        n_estimators=150, max_depth=10, min_samples_split=5, random_state=42
    )
    clf.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)
    
    # 4. Out-of-sample evaluation
    y_pred = clf.predict(X_test_scaled)
    y_proba = clf.predict_proba(X_test_scaled)[:, 1]
    
    print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred))
    print(f"ROC-AUC Score: {roc_auc_score(y_test, y_proba):.4f}")
    return clf, scaler

import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, cross_val_score
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, roc_auc_score

items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to cnn architecture design with mathematical derivations, neural architecture diagrams, production code, and real-world evaluation.

codeSnippet.code:
import cv2
import numpy as np
import torch
import torchvision.transforms as transforms

# Computer vision processing: CNN Architecture Design
def preprocess_and_infer(image_path: str, target_size=(224, 224)) -> torch.Tensor:
    # 1. Load image in BGR and convert to RGB
    img = cv2.imread(image_path)
    img_rgb = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
    
    # 2. PyTorch tensor normalization pipeline (ImageNet stats)
    transform = transforms.Compose([
        transforms.ToPILImage(),
        transforms.Resize(target_size),
        transforms.ToTensor(),
        transforms.Normalize(mean=[0.485, 0.456, 0.406], std=[0.229, 0.224, 0.225])
    ])
    tensor = transform(img_rgb).unsqueeze(0) # Add batch dimension: (1, 3, 224, 224)
    return tensor

from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, roc_auc_score

# Production machine learning implementation: Transfer Learning
def train_and_evaluate_model(X: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.Series):
    # 1. Stratified train/test partition to preserve class distributions
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
        X, y, test_size=0.20, random_state=42, stratify=y
    )
    
    # 2. Fit feature scaler on training data ONLY to prevent data leakage
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
    X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)
    
    # 3. Model instantiation with ensemble regularization
    clf = RandomForestClassifier(
        n_estimators=150, max_depth=10, min_samples_split=5, random_state=42
    )
    clf.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)
    
    # 4. Out-of-sample evaluation
    y_pred = clf.predict(X_test_scaled)
    y_proba = clf.predict_proba(X_test_scaled)[:, 1]
    
    print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred))
    print(f"ROC-AUC Score: {roc_auc_score(y_test, y_proba):.4f}")
    return clf, scaler

codeSnippet.code:
import cv2
import numpy as np
import torch
import torchvision.transforms as transforms

# Computer vision processing: Image Segmentation
def preprocess_and_infer(image_path: str, target_size=(224, 224)) -> torch.Tensor:
    # 1. Load image in BGR and convert to RGB
    img = cv2.imread(image_path)
    img_rgb = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
    
    # 2. PyTorch tensor normalization pipeline (ImageNet stats)
    transform = transforms.Compose([
        transforms.ToPILImage(),
        transforms.Resize(target_size),
        transforms.ToTensor(),
        transforms.Normalize(mean=[0.485, 0.456, 0.406], std=[0.229, 0.224, 0.225])
    ])
    tensor = transform(img_rgb).unsqueeze(0) # Add batch dimension: (1, 3, 224, 224)
    return tensor

import pandas as pd

from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, roc_auc_score

# Production machine learning implementation: Face Detection and Recognition Concepts
def train_and_evaluate_model(X: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.Series):
    # 1. Stratified train/test partition to preserve class distributions
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
        X, y, test_size=0.20, random_state=42, stratify=y
    )
    
    # 2. Fit feature scaler on training data ONLY to prevent data leakage
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
    X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)

        n_estimators=150, max_depth=10, min_samples_split=5, random_state=42
    )

    # 4. Out-of-sample evaluation
    y_pred = clf.predict(X_test_scaled)
    y_proba = clf.predict_proba(X_test_scaled)[:, 1]

items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to vision transformers with mathematical derivations, neural architecture diagrams, production code, and real-world evaluation.

codeSnippet.code:
import cv2
import numpy as np
import torch
import torchvision.transforms as transforms

# Computer vision processing: Vision Transformers
def preprocess_and_infer(image_path: str, target_size=(224, 224)) -> torch.Tensor:
    # 1. Load image in BGR and convert to RGB
    img = cv2.imread(image_path)
    img_rgb = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
    
    # 2. PyTorch tensor normalization pipeline (ImageNet stats)
    transform = transforms.Compose([
        transforms.ToPILImage(),
        transforms.Resize(target_size),
        transforms.ToTensor(),
        transforms.Normalize(mean=[0.485, 0.456, 0.406], std=[0.229, 0.224, 0.225])
    ])
    tensor = transform(img_rgb).unsqueeze(0) # Add batch dimension: (1, 3, 224, 224)
    return tensor

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, cross_val_score
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, roc_auc_score

# Production machine learning implementation: Object Detection Project
def train_and_evaluate_model(X: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.Series):
    # 1. Stratified train/test partition to preserve class distributions
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
        X, y, test_size=0.20, random_state=42, stratify=y
    )
    
    # 2. Fit feature scaler on training data ONLY to prevent data leakage
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
    X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)
    
    # 3. Model instantiation with ensemble regularization
    clf = RandomForestClassifier(
        n_estimators=150, max_depth=10, min_samples_split=5, random_state=42
    )
    clf.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)
    
    # 4. Out-of-sample evaluation
    y_pred = clf.predict(X_test_scaled)
    y_proba = clf.predict_proba(X_test_scaled)[:, 1]
    
    print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred))
    print(f"ROC-AUC Score: {roc_auc_score(y_test, y_proba):.4f}")
    return clf, scaler

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, cross_val_score
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, roc_auc_score

# Production machine learning implementation: Data Augmentation and Error Analysis
def train_and_evaluate_model(X: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.Series):
    # 1. Stratified train/test partition to preserve class distributions
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
        X, y, test_size=0.20, random_state=42, stratify=y
    )
    
    # 2. Fit feature scaler on training data ONLY to prevent data leakage
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
    X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)
    
    # 3. Model instantiation with ensemble regularization
    clf = RandomForestClassifier(
        n_estimators=150, max_depth=10, min_samples_split=5, random_state=42
    )
    clf.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)
    
    # 4. Out-of-sample evaluation
    y_pred = clf.predict(X_test_scaled)
    y_proba = clf.predict_proba(X_test_scaled)[:, 1]
    
    print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred))
    print(f"ROC-AUC Score: {roc_auc_score(y_test, y_proba):.4f}")
    return clf, scaler

codeSnippet.code:
import cv2
import numpy as np
import torch
import torchvision.transforms as transforms

# Computer vision processing: Building a Computer Vision Application
def preprocess_and_infer(image_path: str, target_size=(224, 224)) -> torch.Tensor:
    # 1. Load image in BGR and convert to RGB
    img = cv2.imread(image_path)
    img_rgb = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
    
    # 2. PyTorch tensor normalization pipeline (ImageNet stats)
    transform = transforms.Compose([
        transforms.ToPILImage(),
        transforms.Resize(target_size),
        transforms.ToTensor(),
        transforms.Normalize(mean=[0.485, 0.456, 0.406], std=[0.229, 0.224, 0.225])
    ])
    tensor = transform(img_rgb).unsqueeze(0) # Add batch dimension: (1, 3, 224, 224)
    return tensor

import cv2

    # 1. Load image in BGR and convert to RGB

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, cross_val_score
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, roc_auc_score

# Production machine learning implementation: Convolution Operations and Filters
def train_and_evaluate_model(X: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.Series):
    # 1. Stratified train/test partition to preserve class distributions
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
        X, y, test_size=0.20, random_state=42, stratify=y
    )
    
    # 2. Fit feature scaler on training data ONLY to prevent data leakage
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
    X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)
    
    # 3. Model instantiation with ensemble regularization
    clf = RandomForestClassifier(
        n_estimators=150, max_depth=10, min_samples_split=5, random_state=42
    )
    clf.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)
    
    # 4. Out-of-sample evaluation
    y_pred = clf.predict(X_test_scaled)
    y_proba = clf.predict_proba(X_test_scaled)[:, 1]
    
    print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred))
    print(f"ROC-AUC Score: {roc_auc_score(y_test, y_proba):.4f}")
    return clf, scaler

codeSnippet.code:
import cv2
import numpy as np
import torch
import torchvision.transforms as transforms

# Computer vision processing: CNN Architecture Design
def preprocess_and_infer(image_path: str, target_size=(224, 224)) -> torch.Tensor:
    # 1. Load image in BGR and convert to RGB
    img = cv2.imread(image_path)
    img_rgb = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
    
    # 2. PyTorch tensor normalization pipeline (ImageNet stats)
    transform = transforms.Compose([
        transforms.ToPILImage(),
        transforms.Resize(target_size),
        transforms.ToTensor(),
        transforms.Normalize(mean=[0.485, 0.456, 0.406], std=[0.229, 0.224, 0.225])
    ])
    tensor = transform(img_rgb).unsqueeze(0) # Add batch dimension: (1, 3, 224, 224)
    return tensor

import cv2
import numpy as np
import torch
import torchvision.transforms as transforms

# Computer vision processing: Training CNNs for Image Classification
def preprocess_and_infer(image_path: str, target_size=(224, 224)) -> torch.Tensor:
    # 1. Load image in BGR and convert to RGB
    img = cv2.imread(image_path)
    img_rgb = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
    
    # 2. PyTorch tensor normalization pipeline (ImageNet stats)
    transform = transforms.Compose([
        transforms.ToPILImage(),
        transforms.Resize(target_size),
        transforms.ToTensor(),
        transforms.Normalize(mean=[0.485, 0.456, 0.406], std=[0.229, 0.224, 0.225])
    ])
    tensor = transform(img_rgb).unsqueeze(0) # Add batch dimension: (1, 3, 224, 224)
    return tensor

from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, roc_auc_score

# Production machine learning implementation: Transfer Learning
def train_and_evaluate_model(X: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.Series):
    # 1. Stratified train/test partition to preserve class distributions
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
        X, y, test_size=0.20, random_state=42, stratify=y
    )
    
    # 2. Fit feature scaler on training data ONLY to prevent data leakage
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
    X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)
    
    # 3. Model instantiation with ensemble regularization
    clf = RandomForestClassifier(
        n_estimators=150, max_depth=10, min_samples_split=5, random_state=42
    )
    clf.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)
    
    # 4. Out-of-sample evaluation
    y_pred = clf.predict(X_test_scaled)
    y_proba = clf.predict_proba(X_test_scaled)[:, 1]
    
    print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred))
    print(f"ROC-AUC Score: {roc_auc_score(y_test, y_proba):.4f}")
    return clf, scaler

codeSnippet.code:
import cv2
import numpy as np
import torch
import torchvision.transforms as transforms

# Computer vision processing: Image Segmentation
def preprocess_and_infer(image_path: str, target_size=(224, 224)) -> torch.Tensor:
    # 1. Load image in BGR and convert to RGB
    img = cv2.imread(image_path)
    img_rgb = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
    
    # 2. PyTorch tensor normalization pipeline (ImageNet stats)
    transform = transforms.Compose([
        transforms.ToPILImage(),
        transforms.Resize(target_size),
        transforms.ToTensor(),
        transforms.Normalize(mean=[0.485, 0.456, 0.406], std=[0.229, 0.224, 0.225])
    ])
    tensor = transform(img_rgb).unsqueeze(0) # Add batch dimension: (1, 3, 224, 224)
    return tensor

from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, cross_val_score
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, roc_auc_score

        X, y, test_size=0.20, random_state=42, stratify=y

    X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
    X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)
    
    # 3. Model instantiation with ensemble regularization

        n_estimators=150, max_depth=10, min_samples_split=5, random_state=42

    print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred))

items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to vision transformers with mathematical derivations, neural architecture diagrams, production code, and real-world evaluation.

codeSnippet.code:
import cv2
import numpy as np
import torch
import torchvision.transforms as transforms

# Computer vision processing: Vision Transformers
def preprocess_and_infer(image_path: str, target_size=(224, 224)) -> torch.Tensor:
    # 1. Load image in BGR and convert to RGB
    img = cv2.imread(image_path)
    img_rgb = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
    
    # 2. PyTorch tensor normalization pipeline (ImageNet stats)
    transform = transforms.Compose([
        transforms.ToPILImage(),
        transforms.Resize(target_size),
        transforms.ToTensor(),
        transforms.Normalize(mean=[0.485, 0.456, 0.406], std=[0.229, 0.224, 0.225])
    ])
    tensor = transform(img_rgb).unsqueeze(0) # Add batch dimension: (1, 3, 224, 224)
    return tensor

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, cross_val_score
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, roc_auc_score

# Production machine learning implementation: Object Detection Project
def train_and_evaluate_model(X: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.Series):
    # 1. Stratified train/test partition to preserve class distributions
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
        X, y, test_size=0.20, random_state=42, stratify=y
    )
    
    # 2. Fit feature scaler on training data ONLY to prevent data leakage
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
    X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)
    
    # 3. Model instantiation with ensemble regularization
    clf = RandomForestClassifier(
        n_estimators=150, max_depth=10, min_samples_split=5, random_state=42
    )
    clf.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)
    
    # 4. Out-of-sample evaluation
    y_pred = clf.predict(X_test_scaled)
    y_proba = clf.predict_proba(X_test_scaled)[:, 1]
    
    print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred))
    print(f"ROC-AUC Score: {roc_auc_score(y_test, y_proba):.4f}")
    return clf, scaler

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, cross_val_score
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, roc_auc_score

# Production machine learning implementation: Data Augmentation and Error Analysis
def train_and_evaluate_model(X: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.Series):
    # 1. Stratified train/test partition to preserve class distributions
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
        X, y, test_size=0.20, random_state=42, stratify=y
    )
    
    # 2. Fit feature scaler on training data ONLY to prevent data leakage
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
    X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)
    
    # 3. Model instantiation with ensemble regularization
    clf = RandomForestClassifier(
        n_estimators=150, max_depth=10, min_samples_split=5, random_state=42
    )
    clf.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)
    
    # 4. Out-of-sample evaluation
    y_pred = clf.predict(X_test_scaled)
    y_proba = clf.predict_proba(X_test_scaled)[:, 1]
    
    print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred))
    print(f"ROC-AUC Score: {roc_auc_score(y_test, y_proba):.4f}")
    return clf, scaler

items.title: Building a Computer Vision Application
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to building a computer vision application with mathematical derivations, neural architecture diagrams, production code, and real-world evaluation.

codeSnippet.code:
import cv2
import numpy as np
import torch
import torchvision.transforms as transforms

# Computer vision processing: Building a Computer Vision Application
def preprocess_and_infer(image_path: str, target_size=(224, 224)) -> torch.Tensor:
    # 1. Load image in BGR and convert to RGB
    img = cv2.imread(image_path)
    img_rgb = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
    
    # 2. PyTorch tensor normalization pipeline (ImageNet stats)
    transform = transforms.Compose([
        transforms.ToPILImage(),
        transforms.Resize(target_size),
        transforms.ToTensor(),
        transforms.Normalize(mean=[0.485, 0.456, 0.406], std=[0.229, 0.224, 0.225])
    ])
    tensor = transform(img_rgb).unsqueeze(0) # Add batch dimension: (1, 3, 224, 224)
    return tensor

questions.prompt: Which fundamental objective guides effective model training and parameter optimization in Computer Vision?

options.label: Minimizing training loss to exactly zero while ignoring generalization error
Minimizing empirical loss while regularizing model complexity to optimize out-of-sample generalization
Disabling validation splits to reduce GPU compute usage
Maximizing parameter weights without penalty boundaries

questions.explanation: The core objective in machine learning is structural risk minimization: balancing empirical loss reduction with regularization to ensure the model generalizes effectively to unobserved production distributions.

questions.prompt: In Computer Vision, what is the consequence of severe class imbalance if evaluated solely using standard accuracy?

options.label: The model will automatically recalibrate its probability thresholds without code
A naive model predicting only the majority class can achieve deceptive 99% accuracy while having zero utility
The optimizer will fail to compute gradients during backpropagation
The GPU memory footprint will increase exponentially

questions.explanation: On imbalanced datasets (such as 99% non-fraud vs 1% fraud), a model that predicts non-fraud 100% of the time achieves 99% accuracy while failing completely at detecting fraud. PR-AUC and F1-score are necessary.

questions.prompt: When configuring numerical optimizers like Adam or SGD with momentum in Computer Vision, why is learning rate selection critical?

options.label: Learning rate has no mathematical effect on convergence speed
Too high a rate causes loss divergence; too low a rate causes agonizingly slow convergence or entrapment in poor local minima
Learning rate only applies to linear regression models
A learning rate of 1.0 is universally optimal for all neural network architectures

questions.explanation: Learning rate dictates step size across the loss landscape gradient. Excessive step sizes overshoot minima and diverge, while excessively small step sizes cause stagnation or freeze in suboptimal saddle points.

questions.prompt: In deep learning architectures for Computer Vision, what is the primary role of non-linear activation functions (e.g. ReLU, GELU)?

options.label: To convert 32-bit floats into integer strings
To allow neural networks to approximate non-linear functional relationships and avoid collapsing into a single linear mapping
To reduce the physical storage size of saved checkpoint files
To guarantee that all gradients equal zero during backpropagation

questions.explanation: Without non-linear activations, composing multiple linear layers (W2 * W1 * x) mathematically collapses into a single linear matrix transformation (W_eff * x), preventing the network from learning complex non-linear patterns.

questions.prompt: When deploying models in production for Computer Vision, what is the best strategy for detecting data drift over time?

options.label: Assuming input distributions remain statically identical forever
Continuously monitoring statistical feature divergence (e.g. Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, PSI) between training and live inference payloads
Deleting incoming production payloads after scoring without logging
Disabling API rate limits on inference endpoints

questions.explanation: Production data drift occurs when real-world distributions evolve away from training baseline assumptions. Statistical drift tests (PSI, KS-test) detect these shifts early and trigger automated retraining pipelines.

questions.prompt: Which fundamental objective guides effective model training and parameter optimization in Computer Vision?

options.label: Minimizing training loss to exactly zero while ignoring generalization error
Minimizing empirical loss while regularizing model complexity to optimize out-of-sample generalization
Disabling validation splits to reduce GPU compute usage
Maximizing parameter weights without penalty boundaries

questions.explanation: The core objective in machine learning is structural risk minimization: balancing empirical loss reduction with regularization to ensure the model generalizes effectively to unobserved production distributions.

questions.prompt: In Computer Vision, what is the consequence of severe class imbalance if evaluated solely using standard accuracy?

options.label: The model will automatically recalibrate its probability thresholds without code
A naive model predicting only the majority class can achieve deceptive 99% accuracy while having zero utility
The optimizer will fail to compute gradients during backpropagation
The GPU memory footprint will increase exponentially

questions.explanation: On imbalanced datasets (such as 99% non-fraud vs 1% fraud), a model that predicts non-fraud 100% of the time achieves 99% accuracy while failing completely at detecting fraud. PR-AUC and F1-score are necessary.

questions.prompt: When configuring numerical optimizers like Adam or SGD with momentum in Computer Vision, why is learning rate selection critical?

options.label: Learning rate has no mathematical effect on convergence speed
Too high a rate causes loss divergence; too low a rate causes agonizingly slow convergence or entrapment in poor local minima
Learning rate only applies to linear regression models
A learning rate of 1.0 is universally optimal for all neural network architectures

questions.explanation: Learning rate dictates step size across the loss landscape gradient. Excessive step sizes overshoot minima and diverge, while excessively small step sizes cause stagnation or freeze in suboptimal saddle points.

questions.prompt: In deep learning architectures for Computer Vision, what is the primary role of non-linear activation functions (e.g. ReLU, GELU)?

options.label: To convert 32-bit floats into integer strings
To allow neural networks to approximate non-linear functional relationships and avoid collapsing into a single linear mapping
To reduce the physical storage size of saved checkpoint files
To guarantee that all gradients equal zero during backpropagation

questions.explanation: Without non-linear activations, composing multiple linear layers (W2 * W1 * x) mathematically collapses into a single linear matrix transformation (W_eff * x), preventing the network from learning complex non-linear patterns.

questions.prompt: When deploying models in production for Computer Vision, what is the best strategy for detecting data drift over time?

options.label: Assuming input distributions remain statically identical forever
Continuously monitoring statistical feature divergence (e.g. Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, PSI) between training and live inference payloads
Deleting incoming production payloads after scoring without logging
Disabling API rate limits on inference endpoints

questions.explanation: Production data drift occurs when real-world distributions evolve away from training baseline assumptions. Statistical drift tests (PSI, KS-test) detect these shifts early and trigger automated retraining pipelines.

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, cross_val_score
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, roc_auc_score

# Production machine learning implementation: What Is Natural Language Processing?
def train_and_evaluate_model(X: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.Series):
    # 1. Stratified train/test partition to preserve class distributions
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
        X, y, test_size=0.20, random_state=42, stratify=y
    )
    
    # 2. Fit feature scaler on training data ONLY to prevent data leakage
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
    X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)
    
    # 3. Model instantiation with ensemble regularization
    clf = RandomForestClassifier(
        n_estimators=150, max_depth=10, min_samples_split=5, random_state=42
    )
    clf.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)
    
    # 4. Out-of-sample evaluation
    y_pred = clf.predict(X_test_scaled)
    y_proba = clf.predict_proba(X_test_scaled)[:, 1]
    
    print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred))
    print(f"ROC-AUC Score: {roc_auc_score(y_test, y_proba):.4f}")
    return clf, scaler

items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to text processing and normalization with mathematical derivations, neural architecture diagrams, production code, and real-world evaluation.

codeSnippet.code:
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForSequenceClassification
import torch

# Modern Transformer NLP pipeline: Text Processing and Normalization
MODEL_NAME = "distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAME)
model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAME)

def classify_text_sentiment(text: str) -> dict:
    inputs = tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt", truncation=True, max_length=512)
    with torch.no_grad():
        logits = model(**inputs).logits
        probabilities = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1).squeeze().tolist()
        
    return {
        "negative_score": round(probabilities[0], 4),
        "positive_score": round(probabilities[1], 4),
        "prediction": "POSITIVE" if probabilities[1] > probabilities[0] else "NEGATIVE"
    }

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, cross_val_score
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, roc_auc_score

# Production machine learning implementation: Stop Words, Stemming and Lemmatization
def train_and_evaluate_model(X: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.Series):
    # 1. Stratified train/test partition to preserve class distributions
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
        X, y, test_size=0.20, random_state=42, stratify=y
    )
    
    # 2. Fit feature scaler on training data ONLY to prevent data leakage
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
    X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)
    
    # 3. Model instantiation with ensemble regularization
    clf = RandomForestClassifier(
        n_estimators=150, max_depth=10, min_samples_split=5, random_state=42
    )
    clf.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)
    
    # 4. Out-of-sample evaluation
    y_pred = clf.predict(X_test_scaled)
    y_proba = clf.predict_proba(X_test_scaled)[:, 1]
    
    print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred))
    print(f"ROC-AUC Score: {roc_auc_score(y_test, y_proba):.4f}")
    return clf, scaler

codeSnippet.code:
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForSequenceClassification
import torch

# Modern Transformer NLP pipeline: Text Clustering
MODEL_NAME = "distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAME)
model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAME)

def classify_text_sentiment(text: str) -> dict:
    inputs = tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt", truncation=True, max_length=512)
    with torch.no_grad():
        logits = model(**inputs).logits
        probabilities = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1).squeeze().tolist()
        
    return {
        "negative_score": round(probabilities[0], 4),
        "positive_score": round(probabilities[1], 4),
        "prediction": "POSITIVE" if probabilities[1] > probabilities[0] else "NEGATIVE"
    }

import torch

    }

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, cross_val_score
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, roc_auc_score

# Production machine learning implementation: Sequential Data and Language Modeling
def train_and_evaluate_model(X: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.Series):
    # 1. Stratified train/test partition to preserve class distributions
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
        X, y, test_size=0.20, random_state=42, stratify=y
    )
    
    # 2. Fit feature scaler on training data ONLY to prevent data leakage
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
    X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)
    
    # 3. Model instantiation with ensemble regularization
    clf = RandomForestClassifier(
        n_estimators=150, max_depth=10, min_samples_split=5, random_state=42
    )
    clf.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)
    
    # 4. Out-of-sample evaluation
    y_pred = clf.predict(X_test_scaled)
    y_proba = clf.predict_proba(X_test_scaled)[:, 1]
    
    print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred))
    print(f"ROC-AUC Score: {roc_auc_score(y_test, y_proba):.4f}")
    return clf, scaler

items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to recurrent neural networks with mathematical derivations, neural architecture diagrams, production code, and real-world evaluation.

codeSnippet.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.optim as optim

# Production PyTorch architecture: Recurrent Neural Networks
class DeepClassifier(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_dim: int, hidden_dim: int, num_classes: int):
        super().__init__()
        self.network = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(hidden_dim),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Dropout(p=0.25),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim // 2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim // 2, num_classes)
        )

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return self.network(x)

# Training step with AdamW optimizer & Cross-Entropy Loss
device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
model = DeepClassifier(input_dim=64, hidden_dim=128, num_classes=5).to(device)
criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
optimizer = optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3, weight_decay=1e-4)

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, cross_val_score
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, roc_auc_score

# Production machine learning implementation: LSTMs and GRUs
def train_and_evaluate_model(X: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.Series):
    # 1. Stratified train/test partition to preserve class distributions
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
        X, y, test_size=0.20, random_state=42, stratify=y
    )
    
    # 2. Fit feature scaler on training data ONLY to prevent data leakage
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
    X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)
    
    # 3. Model instantiation with ensemble regularization
    clf = RandomForestClassifier(
        n_estimators=150, max_depth=10, min_samples_split=5, random_state=42
    )
    clf.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)
    
    # 4. Out-of-sample evaluation
    y_pred = clf.predict(X_test_scaled)
    y_proba = clf.predict_proba(X_test_scaled)[:, 1]
    
    print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred))
    print(f"ROC-AUC Score: {roc_auc_score(y_test, y_proba):.4f}")
    return clf, scaler

items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to transformer architecture with mathematical derivations, neural architecture diagrams, production code, and real-world evaluation.

codeSnippet.code:
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForSequenceClassification
import torch

# Modern Transformer NLP pipeline: Transformer Architecture
MODEL_NAME = "distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAME)
model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAME)

def classify_text_sentiment(text: str) -> dict:
    inputs = tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt", truncation=True, max_length=512)
    with torch.no_grad():
        logits = model(**inputs).logits
        probabilities = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1).squeeze().tolist()
        
    return {
        "negative_score": round(probabilities[0], 4),
        "positive_score": round(probabilities[1], 4),
        "prediction": "POSITIVE" if probabilities[1] > probabilities[0] else "NEGATIVE"
    }

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, cross_val_score
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, roc_auc_score

# Production machine learning implementation: What Is Natural Language Processing?
def train_and_evaluate_model(X: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.Series):
    # 1. Stratified train/test partition to preserve class distributions
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
        X, y, test_size=0.20, random_state=42, stratify=y
    )
    
    # 2. Fit feature scaler on training data ONLY to prevent data leakage
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
    X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)
    
    # 3. Model instantiation with ensemble regularization
    clf = RandomForestClassifier(
        n_estimators=150, max_depth=10, min_samples_split=5, random_state=42
    )
    clf.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)
    
    # 4. Out-of-sample evaluation
    y_pred = clf.predict(X_test_scaled)
    y_proba = clf.predict_proba(X_test_scaled)[:, 1]
    
    print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred))
    print(f"ROC-AUC Score: {roc_auc_score(y_test, y_proba):.4f}")
    return clf, scaler

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, cross_val_score
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, roc_auc_score

# Production machine learning implementation: Stop Words, Stemming and Lemmatization
def train_and_evaluate_model(X: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.Series):
    # 1. Stratified train/test partition to preserve class distributions
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
        X, y, test_size=0.20, random_state=42, stratify=y
    )
    
    # 2. Fit feature scaler on training data ONLY to prevent data leakage
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
    X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)
    
    # 3. Model instantiation with ensemble regularization
    clf = RandomForestClassifier(
        n_estimators=150, max_depth=10, min_samples_split=5, random_state=42
    )
    clf.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)
    
    # 4. Out-of-sample evaluation
    y_pred = clf.predict(X_test_scaled)
    y_proba = clf.predict_proba(X_test_scaled)[:, 1]
    
    print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred))
    print(f"ROC-AUC Score: {roc_auc_score(y_test, y_proba):.4f}")
    return clf, scaler

codeSnippet.code:
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForSequenceClassification
import torch

# Modern Transformer NLP pipeline: Text Clustering
MODEL_NAME = "distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAME)
model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAME)

def classify_text_sentiment(text: str) -> dict:
    inputs = tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt", truncation=True, max_length=512)
    with torch.no_grad():
        logits = model(**inputs).logits
        probabilities = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1).squeeze().tolist()
        
    return {
        "negative_score": round(probabilities[0], 4),
        "positive_score": round(probabilities[1], 4),
        "prediction": "POSITIVE" if probabilities[1] > probabilities[0] else "NEGATIVE"
    }

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, cross_val_score
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, roc_auc_score

# Production machine learning implementation: Sequential Data and Language Modeling
def train_and_evaluate_model(X: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.Series):
    # 1. Stratified train/test partition to preserve class distributions
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
        X, y, test_size=0.20, random_state=42, stratify=y
    )
    
    # 2. Fit feature scaler on training data ONLY to prevent data leakage
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
    X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)
    
    # 3. Model instantiation with ensemble regularization
    clf = RandomForestClassifier(
        n_estimators=150, max_depth=10, min_samples_split=5, random_state=42
    )
    clf.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)
    
    # 4. Out-of-sample evaluation
    y_pred = clf.predict(X_test_scaled)
    y_proba = clf.predict_proba(X_test_scaled)[:, 1]
    
    print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred))
    print(f"ROC-AUC Score: {roc_auc_score(y_test, y_proba):.4f}")
    return clf, scaler

codeSnippet.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.optim as optim

# Production PyTorch architecture: Recurrent Neural Networks
class DeepClassifier(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_dim: int, hidden_dim: int, num_classes: int):
        super().__init__()
        self.network = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(hidden_dim),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Dropout(p=0.25),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim // 2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim // 2, num_classes)
        )

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return self.network(x)

# Training step with AdamW optimizer & Cross-Entropy Loss
device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
model = DeepClassifier(input_dim=64, hidden_dim=128, num_classes=5).to(device)
criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
optimizer = optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3, weight_decay=1e-4)

codeSnippet.code:
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForSequenceClassification
import torch

# Modern Transformer NLP pipeline: Transformer Architecture
MODEL_NAME = "distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAME)
model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAME)

def classify_text_sentiment(text: str) -> dict:
    inputs = tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt", truncation=True, max_length=512)
    with torch.no_grad():
        logits = model(**inputs).logits
        probabilities = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1).squeeze().tolist()
        
    return {
        "negative_score": round(probabilities[0], 4),
        "positive_score": round(probabilities[1], 4),
        "prediction": "POSITIVE" if probabilities[1] > probabilities[0] else "NEGATIVE"
    }

Disabling validation splits to reduce GPU compute usage
Maximizing parameter weights without penalty boundaries

questions.prompt: In Natural Language Processing, what is the consequence of severe class imbalance if evaluated solely using standard accuracy?

A naive model predicting only the majority class can achieve deceptive 99% accuracy while having zero utility
The optimizer will fail to compute gradients during backpropagation
The GPU memory footprint will increase exponentially

questions.explanation: On imbalanced datasets (such as 99% non-fraud vs 1% fraud), a model that predicts non-fraud 100% of the time achieves 99% accuracy while failing completely at detecting fraud. PR-AUC and F1-score are necessary.

questions.prompt: When configuring numerical optimizers like Adam or SGD with momentum in Natural Language Processing, why is learning rate selection critical?

options.label: Learning rate has no mathematical effect on convergence speed
Too high a rate causes loss divergence; too low a rate causes agonizingly slow convergence or entrapment in poor local minima
Learning rate only applies to linear regression models
A learning rate of 1.0 is universally optimal for all neural network architectures

questions.explanation: Learning rate dictates step size across the loss landscape gradient. Excessive step sizes overshoot minima and diverge, while excessively small step sizes cause stagnation or freeze in suboptimal saddle points.

questions.prompt: In deep learning architectures for Natural Language Processing, what is the primary role of non-linear activation functions (e.g. ReLU, GELU)?

To allow neural networks to approximate non-linear functional relationships and avoid collapsing into a single linear mapping
To reduce the physical storage size of saved checkpoint files
To guarantee that all gradients equal zero during backpropagation

questions.explanation: Without non-linear activations, composing multiple linear layers (W2 * W1 * x) mathematically collapses into a single linear matrix transformation (W_eff * x), preventing the network from learning complex non-linear patterns.

Deleting incoming production payloads after scoring without logging
Disabling API rate limits on inference endpoints

questions.explanation: Production data drift occurs when real-world distributions evolve away from training baseline assumptions. Statistical drift tests (PSI, KS-test) detect these shifts early and trigger automated retraining pipelines.

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, cross_val_score
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, roc_auc_score

# Production machine learning implementation: What Is Generative AI?
def train_and_evaluate_model(X: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.Series):
    # 1. Stratified train/test partition to preserve class distributions
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
        X, y, test_size=0.20, random_state=42, stratify=y
    )
    
    # 2. Fit feature scaler on training data ONLY to prevent data leakage
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
    X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)
    
    # 3. Model instantiation with ensemble regularization
    clf = RandomForestClassifier(
        n_estimators=150, max_depth=10, min_samples_split=5, random_state=42
    )
    clf.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)
    
    # 4. Out-of-sample evaluation
    y_pred = clf.predict(X_test_scaled)
    y_proba = clf.predict_proba(X_test_scaled)[:, 1]
    
    print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred))
    print(f"ROC-AUC Score: {roc_auc_score(y_test, y_proba):.4f}")
    return clf, scaler

import cv2

import torch
import torchvision.transforms as transforms

# Computer vision processing: Text, Image, Audio and Video Generation
def preprocess_and_infer(image_path: str, target_size=(224, 224)) -> torch.Tensor:
    # 1. Load image in BGR and convert to RGB
    img = cv2.imread(image_path)
    img_rgb = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
    
    # 2. PyTorch tensor normalization pipeline (ImageNet stats)
    transform = transforms.Compose([
        transforms.ToPILImage(),
        transforms.Resize(target_size),
        transforms.ToTensor(),

    ])

    return tensor

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, cross_val_score
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, roc_auc_score

# Production machine learning implementation: Capabilities and Limitations of Generative AI
def train_and_evaluate_model(X: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.Series):
    # 1. Stratified train/test partition to preserve class distributions
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
        X, y, test_size=0.20, random_state=42, stratify=y
    )
    
    # 2. Fit feature scaler on training data ONLY to prevent data leakage
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
    X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)
    
    # 3. Model instantiation with ensemble regularization
    clf = RandomForestClassifier(
        n_estimators=150, max_depth=10, min_samples_split=5, random_state=42
    )
    clf.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)
    
    # 4. Out-of-sample evaluation
    y_pred = clf.predict(X_test_scaled)
    y_proba = clf.predict_proba(X_test_scaled)[:, 1]
    
    print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred))
    print(f"ROC-AUC Score: {roc_auc_score(y_test, y_proba):.4f}")
    return clf, scaler

codeSnippet.code:
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForSequenceClassification
import torch

# Modern Transformer NLP pipeline: Tokens and Tokenization
MODEL_NAME = "distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAME)
model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAME)

def classify_text_sentiment(text: str) -> dict:
    inputs = tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt", truncation=True, max_length=512)
    with torch.no_grad():
        logits = model(**inputs).logits
        probabilities = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1).squeeze().tolist()
        
    return {
        "negative_score": round(probabilities[0], 4),
        "positive_score": round(probabilities[1], 4),
        "prediction": "POSITIVE" if probabilities[1] > probabilities[0] else "NEGATIVE"
    }

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, cross_val_score
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, roc_auc_score

# Production machine learning implementation: Self-Attention and Multi-Head Attention
def train_and_evaluate_model(X: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.Series):
    # 1. Stratified train/test partition to preserve class distributions
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
        X, y, test_size=0.20, random_state=42, stratify=y
    )
    
    # 2. Fit feature scaler on training data ONLY to prevent data leakage
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
    X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)
    
    # 3. Model instantiation with ensemble regularization
    clf = RandomForestClassifier(
        n_estimators=150, max_depth=10, min_samples_split=5, random_state=42
    )
    clf.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)
    
    # 4. Out-of-sample evaluation
    y_pred = clf.predict(X_test_scaled)
    y_proba = clf.predict_proba(X_test_scaled)[:, 1]
    
    print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred))
    print(f"ROC-AUC Score: {roc_auc_score(y_test, y_proba):.4f}")
    return clf, scaler

codeSnippet.code:
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForSequenceClassification
import torch

MODEL_NAME = "distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAME)
model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAME)

def classify_text_sentiment(text: str) -> dict:
    inputs = tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt", truncation=True, max_length=512)
    with torch.no_grad():
        logits = model(**inputs).logits
        probabilities = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1).squeeze().tolist()
        
    return {
        "negative_score": round(probabilities[0], 4),
        "positive_score": round(probabilities[1], 4),
        "prediction": "POSITIVE" if probabilities[1] > probabilities[0] else "NEGATIVE"
    }

from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForSequenceClassification
import torch

# Modern Transformer NLP pipeline: Instruction, Context and Constraints
MODEL_NAME = "distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAME)
model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAME)

def classify_text_sentiment(text: str) -> dict:
    inputs = tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt", truncation=True, max_length=512)
    with torch.no_grad():
        logits = model(**inputs).logits
        probabilities = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1).squeeze().tolist()
        
    return {
        "negative_score": round(probabilities[0], 4),
        "positive_score": round(probabilities[1], 4),
        "prediction": "POSITIVE" if probabilities[1] > probabilities[0] else "NEGATIVE"
    }

items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to cost, latency and token management with mathematical derivations, neural architecture diagrams, production code, and real-world evaluation.

codeSnippet.code:
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForSequenceClassification
import torch

# Modern Transformer NLP pipeline: Cost, Latency and Token Management
MODEL_NAME = "distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAME)
model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAME)

def classify_text_sentiment(text: str) -> dict:
    inputs = tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt", truncation=True, max_length=512)
    with torch.no_grad():
        logits = model(**inputs).logits
        probabilities = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1).squeeze().tolist()
        
    return {
        "negative_score": round(probabilities[0], 4),
        "positive_score": round(probabilities[1], 4),
        "prediction": "POSITIVE" if probabilities[1] > probabilities[0] else "NEGATIVE"
    }

items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to error handling and retry strategies with mathematical derivations, neural architecture diagrams, production code, and real-world evaluation.

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, cross_val_score
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, roc_auc_score

# Production machine learning implementation: Error Handling and Retry Strategies
def train_and_evaluate_model(X: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.Series):
    # 1. Stratified train/test partition to preserve class distributions
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
        X, y, test_size=0.20, random_state=42, stratify=y
    )
    
    # 2. Fit feature scaler on training data ONLY to prevent data leakage
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
    X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)
    
    # 3. Model instantiation with ensemble regularization
    clf = RandomForestClassifier(
        n_estimators=150, max_depth=10, min_samples_split=5, random_state=42
    )
    clf.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)
    
    # 4. Out-of-sample evaluation
    y_pred = clf.predict(X_test_scaled)
    y_proba = clf.predict_proba(X_test_scaled)[:, 1]
    
    print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred))
    print(f"ROC-AUC Score: {roc_auc_score(y_test, y_proba):.4f}")
    return clf, scaler

items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to building an llm-powered application with mathematical derivations, neural architecture diagrams, production code, and real-world evaluation.

codeSnippet.code:
from openai import OpenAI
import os

client = OpenAI(api_key=os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY"))

# Production AI Agent & RAG reasoning: Building an LLM-Powered Application
def execute_agent_reasoning(user_goal: str, retrieved_context: list[str]) -> str:
    system_prompt = (
        "You are an autonomous AI research scientist. "
        "Use ONLY the grounded context provided below to formulate your structured answer. "
        "Cite specific source documents and state confidence intervals."
    )
    context_str = "\n---\n".join(retrieved_context)
    
    response = client.chat.completions.create(
        model="gpt-4o",
        temperature=0.1,
        messages=[
            {"role": "system", "content": system_prompt},
            {"role": "user", "content": f"Context:\n{context_str}\n\nGoal:\n{user_goal}"}
        ]
    )
    return response.choices[0].message.content

import cv2

import torch
import torchvision.transforms as transforms

# Computer vision processing: Text, Image, Audio and Video Generation
def preprocess_and_infer(image_path: str, target_size=(224, 224)) -> torch.Tensor:
    # 1. Load image in BGR and convert to RGB
    img = cv2.imread(image_path)
    img_rgb = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
    
    # 2. PyTorch tensor normalization pipeline (ImageNet stats)
    transform = transforms.Compose([
        transforms.ToPILImage(),
        transforms.Resize(target_size),
        transforms.ToTensor(),
        transforms.Normalize(mean=[0.485, 0.456, 0.406], std=[0.229, 0.224, 0.225])
    ])
    tensor = transform(img_rgb).unsqueeze(0) # Add batch dimension: (1, 3, 224, 224)
    return tensor

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, cross_val_score
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, roc_auc_score

# Production machine learning implementation: Embeddings and Vector Representations
def train_and_evaluate_model(X: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.Series):
    # 1. Stratified train/test partition to preserve class distributions
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
        X, y, test_size=0.20, random_state=42, stratify=y
    )
    
    # 2. Fit feature scaler on training data ONLY to prevent data leakage
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
    X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)
    
    # 3. Model instantiation with ensemble regularization
    clf = RandomForestClassifier(
        n_estimators=150, max_depth=10, min_samples_split=5, random_state=42
    )
    clf.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)
    
    # 4. Out-of-sample evaluation
    y_pred = clf.predict(X_test_scaled)
    y_proba = clf.predict_proba(X_test_scaled)[:, 1]
    
    print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred))
    print(f"ROC-AUC Score: {roc_auc_score(y_test, y_proba):.4f}")
    return clf, scaler

codeSnippet.code:
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForSequenceClassification
import torch

# Modern Transformer NLP pipeline: Pretraining and Next-Token Prediction
MODEL_NAME = "distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAME)
model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAME)

def classify_text_sentiment(text: str) -> dict:
    inputs = tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt", truncation=True, max_length=512)
    with torch.no_grad():
        logits = model(**inputs).logits
        probabilities = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1).squeeze().tolist()
        
    return {
        "negative_score": round(probabilities[0], 4),
        "positive_score": round(probabilities[1], 4),
        "prediction": "POSITIVE" if probabilities[1] > probabilities[0] else "NEGATIVE"
    }

codeSnippet.code:
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForSequenceClassification
import torch

# Modern Transformer NLP pipeline: Cost, Latency and Token Management
MODEL_NAME = "distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAME)
model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAME)

def classify_text_sentiment(text: str) -> dict:
    inputs = tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt", truncation=True, max_length=512)
    with torch.no_grad():
        logits = model(**inputs).logits
        probabilities = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1).squeeze().tolist()
        
    return {
        "negative_score": round(probabilities[0], 4),
        "positive_score": round(probabilities[1], 4),
        "prediction": "POSITIVE" if probabilities[1] > probabilities[0] else "NEGATIVE"
    }

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, cross_val_score
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, roc_auc_score

# Production machine learning implementation: Error Handling and Retry Strategies
def train_and_evaluate_model(X: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.Series):
    # 1. Stratified train/test partition to preserve class distributions
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
        X, y, test_size=0.20, random_state=42, stratify=y
    )
    
    # 2. Fit feature scaler on training data ONLY to prevent data leakage
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
    X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)
    
    # 3. Model instantiation with ensemble regularization
    clf = RandomForestClassifier(
        n_estimators=150, max_depth=10, min_samples_split=5, random_state=42
    )
    clf.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)
    
    # 4. Out-of-sample evaluation
    y_pred = clf.predict(X_test_scaled)
    y_proba = clf.predict_proba(X_test_scaled)[:, 1]
    
    print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred))
    print(f"ROC-AUC Score: {roc_auc_score(y_test, y_proba):.4f}")
    return clf, scaler
